articles.title: Toolpath Reversal
articles.summary: Alternating cut bands with crescent entry marks and scalloped exit edges. A fine horizontal-brick shimmer that reads as machined, rowed grain; crescents blur into lines of light.
articles.what: Alternating interrupted cuts with entry crescents, exit scallops, protected lands and compact burrs. Up close: Staggered brick-like rows of rectangular cells, about 30 x 15 px, each holding a smile-shaped crescent cut with a small round burr dot. Rows alternate in direction like a milling pass. On satin the crescents glow as bright arcs; on metallic dots and rings sparkle. From a distance: A fine horizontal-brick shimmer that reads as machined, rowed grain; crescents blur into lines of light. It changes the shine only, never the colour. Channels it touches: metal, roughness, clearcoat. Group: Machined & Brushed (Surface library tab of the spec overlay picker). Texture detail: micro.
when: Best on: body, sides, under stripes.
how: Click a zone card and expand SPEC OVERLAYS.
Click + ADD SPEC OVERLAY, open the Surface library tab and the group "Machined & Brushed", or search for "Toolpath Reversal".
Click it, then click Add this overlay in the Inspect surface window.
Set Strength (default 50%) and tick the Metallic, Roughness and Clearcoat boxes you want.
Use Size and Rotation to make the texture finer, then render.
tips: Hood, sides and splitter; the brick rows read on broad panels
Avoid tiny panels, it gets busy
Numbers stay readable; the cells add busy rows behind them, bold numbers best.
Bright crescent arcs in the highlight, a clean milled satin look
Pairs well with: metallic, chrome, gloss.
pitfalls: Not brushed metal: separate crescent cuts in brick rows, not continuous lines
Not Fish Scale: crescents sit in rectangular brick cells, not overlapping round scales
Avoid: banding clashes with stripes, too busy on small panels.
articles.intent_note: A spec pattern changes the shine only: metal, roughness and clearcoat, never the paint colour.
articles.paint_advice: It cannot recolour anything. Metal added to a light paint looks bright; metal added to a dark paint stays dark, because metal reflection inherits the paint colour. Pair it with a paint that gives the gloss difference something to show on.

combos.why: Up to five overlays stack in order; a strong overlay can wash out the ones below it.
The blend mode decides how this overlay meets the base shine. Normal is the safe start.
Coat values 1 to 15 and roughness under 15 on non-chrome pixels are raised to safe values on export.

examples.title: Add it as an overlay
examples.goal: Layer Toolpath Reversal over a base finish.
examples.result: The shine of the zone gets this texture while the colours stay put.

articles.title: Weld-Pool Archive
articles.summary: Dense scalloped weld beads with heat toes and spatter; high coverage, chrome-like breaks. A fine dense rowed grain, like fine corduroy or knurled-weld texture; the beads blur into a lively busy sheen.
articles.what: Three-sided corner seams contain overlapping scalloped weld beads, heat-affected toes, spatter and interrupted polished breaks. Up close: Very dense, tightly packed rows of tiny scalloped bead shapes, about 8-12 px, that look like rows of tiny type or stacked weld ripples with round spatter dots between rows. Bright scallop tops glint in the highlight on both bases; on satin it looks grainier, on metallic cleaner. From a distance: A fine dense rowed grain, like fine corduroy or knurled-weld texture; the beads blur into a lively busy sheen. It changes the shine only, never the colour. Channels it touches: metal, roughness, clearcoat. Group: Machined & Brushed (Surface library tab of the spec overlay picker). Texture detail: micro.
how: Click a zone card and expand SPEC OVERLAYS.

Use Size and Rotation to make the texture finer, then render.
tips: Sides, bumpers and rockers: fabricated look suits lower panels
Avoid small panels or under fine stripes, it overwhelms
Numbers stay readable but the dense grain behind them is busy; bold numbers best.
Grainy glittery rows in the highlight; rough weld-seam texture
Pairs well with: chrome, metallic, matte.
pitfalls: Not Weld Stack Rainbow: this is dense tiny scallops in packed rows, that one is thin dashed bead lines
Not a paint weld graphic: shine only, no colour
Avoid: overwhelms small panels, busy under stripes.
